paper_title: Stochastic fluctuations of bosonic dark matter
coupling_convention: g_aNN in GeV^-1 (axion-nucleon gradient coupling), values as plotted on the log10 g_aNN [GeV^-1] axis
notes: This is a theoretical/methodological paper, not a new experimental search. It shows that previous bosonic DM constraints (nEDM, CASPEr-ZULF-Comagnetometer, CASPEr-ZULF-Sidebands for axion-nucleon coupling gaNN; and dilaton/scalar clock-comparison experiments for d_e) were overestimated by factors ~3-10 because they neglected stochastic amplitude fluctuations of the virialized ultralight field when T << tau_c. The paper rescales existing published limits (correction factor ~8.4 for pseudoscalar wind-type couplings, ~2.7-3.0 for scalar couplings) rather than presenting new experimental data. No numerical table of limits is provided; the revised exclusion curves (Figs. 3-4) are rescaled versions of prior experiments' results. The pre-analysis hint of AxionEDM is incorrect - the plots show gaNN (axion-nucleon gradient coupling, GeV^-1) and dilaton d_e, but since multiple coupling types are corrected and no new limit is derived here, coupling_type is set to null. rho_DM = 0.4 GeV/cm^3 is the assumed local density in the underlying analyses. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Paper: Centers et al., 'Stochastic fluctuations of bosonic dark matter'. Fig. 3 shows the corrected (stochastic, green) constraint on g_aNN vs the original deterministic (gray) constraint. Traced the GREEN stochastic boundary: CASPEr-ZULF Comagnetometer segment (1e-22 to ~1e-16.2 eV, factor ~8.4 weaker than deterministic, with MC roll-off below ~1e-21 eV) and CASPEr-ZULF Sidebands segment (~1e-16 to 1e-13 eV, rising ~linearly with mass on log-log). Hint suggested AxionEDM (d_n in e cm), but the plotted y-axis is clearly log10 g_aNN [GeV^-1] (nucleon coupling), so AxionNeutron was chosen and values emitted as plotted per the plotted-values contract; confidence reduced accordingly.
